classification.difficultyReason: Express two solution volumes using one unknown and balance their percentage contributions to the total acid volume.

content.prompt: Solution A contains 40% of concentrated acid and solution B contains 60% of the same concentrated acid. How many cubic centimetres of each type are needed to produce $1000\text{ cm}^{3}$ of mixture containing 55% concentrated acid?

answer.short:
Solution A: $250\text{ cm}^{3}$. Solution B: $750\text{ cm}^{3}$.

Balance the acid contributed by the two solutions against 55% of the total volume.
answer.worked:
Let $x\text{ cm}^{3}$ be the volume of solution A. The volume of solution B is $(1000-x)\text{ cm}^{3}$. Equate the volumes of concentrated acid:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{40x}{100}+\frac{60(1000-x)}{100}&=\frac{55\times1000}{100}\\40x+60(1000-x)&=55000\\40x+60000-60x&=55000\\60000&=55000+20x\\5000&=20x\\x&=250\end{align*}$$
The volume of solution B is $1000-250=750\text{ cm}^{3}$. Therefore, use $250\text{ cm}^{3}$ of solution A and $750\text{ cm}^{3}$ of solution B.
